clean.tx: & wicode Þær Þa hwile [Þe man Þa burg worthe & getimbrode].
clean.tl: … and camped there at the time that/while the fortress was worked on and built.

clean.tx: ic ne secge
clean.tl: I do not say.

clean.tx: & het forbærnan þæt gewrit [CP 0i þe hit ti on awriten wæs]
clean.tl: and ordered to burn the writ that it was written in

clean.tx: Đonne hie lecgeað ða tiglan beforan hie [CP 0i þe him beboden wæs [CP 0i ðæt hie sceoldon ða ceastre Hierusalem ti on awritan]]
clean.tl: Then they put in front of them the tiles that they were ordered to draw the city of Jerusalem on.

clean.tx: þæt þær nane oðre on ne sæton
clean.tl: that no others sat (on) there

clean.tx: þa genealæhte him an man to
clean.tl: then a man approached him

clean.tx: & on oþerre wæs an gewrit, þær wæron on awritene ealra þara ricestena monna noman
clean.tl: and in the other was a writ, on which were written the names of all the richest men

clean.tx: to beteran tidun þonne we nu on sint
clean.tl: in better times than we are in now

clean.tx: …, sua him læs licað ðæt ðæt hie to gelaðode sindon,
clean.tl: …, the less they are pleased with that to which they are called

clean.tx: Ond þonne Norþanhymbra mægþe þæm Ceolwulf se cyning in cynedome ofer is,
clean.tl: And in the province of Northumbria, over which King Ceolwulf reigns.

clean.tx: Swylce eac ealle ða hrægl, þa ðe he mid gegearwad wæs,
clean.tl: Also all the robes in which he was attired, …

clean.tx: Hit byð dysig æt man speca ær one he ænce
clean.tl: It be foolish that a man speaks before he thinks.' (c1100. Prov 1 [Cox]: 2.2, via )

clean.tx: Wið stede & for gebinde, heortes hær beoð swiðe gode mid to smeocanne wifmannum
clean.tl: Against strangury and constipation, hairs of the hart be very good for women to fumigate with.' (c1025. Med 1.1 [de Vriend]: 3.16, via )

clean.tx: Og er hann hungraði, vildi hann matar neyta. En á meðan þeir voru að búa til, leið yfir hann brjósthöfgi og sá himininn opinn og ofan fara að sér disk nokkurn mikinn svo sem línlak í fjórum hyrningum upp bundinn.
clean.tl: He became hungry and wanted something to eat; but while it was being prepared, he fell into a trance, and saw that the heavens were open, and that something like a great sail was descending, let down by its four corners towards the earth.' (Acts 10; Nýja testamenti Odds, Íslenskt textasafn: )

clean.tx: forþæm he wenð þæt [he] [hi] þonne ealle hæbbe
clean.tl: because he know that he then had them all' [coboeth, Bo: 24.56.16.1031];

clean.tx: Gif ðonne [hwelc mon] forbireð his synna
clean.tl: If anyone then refrains from his sins' [cocura, CP: 37.265.1.1719];

clean.tx: Wæs þa sum Godes þegen binnon þære byri
clean.tl: There was a man of God in the city.

clean.tx: Þa foron forð oþ hi comon to Lundenbyrig & ða mid þam burhwarum & mid þam fultume ðe him westan com foran east to Beamfleote; Wæs ða Hæsten þær cumen mid his herge þe ær æt Middeltune sæt
clean.tl: Then they went forth until they reached London and then they went east to Benfleet with the citizens and with the reinforcements that came to them from the west. Then Hasten came there with his army, which had previously stayed at Middletown'. [ChronC (O'Brien_O'Keeffe): [038400 (894.35)]]

clean.tx: Þa eode he, ure dryhten Crist, ut beforan þa Iudeas. Hæfde he þaþyrnenne coronan on his heafde, & mid þam readan hrægle gegyred wæs. Þa cwæð he, Pilatus, to Iudeum:Ecce homo
clean.tl: Then he, our Lord Christ, went out before the Jews. He had a crown of thorns on his head and he was wearing a red robe. Then he, Pontius Pilate, said to the Jews: Ecce homo.' [HomS_24_ (ScraggVerc_1): [009500 (159)]–[009700 (161)]]

clean.tx: Weaxe ge nu
clean.tl: Grow now.

clean.tx: Mæg gehyran se ðe wyle be þam halgan mædene Eugenian …
clean.tl: Let everyone interested hear about the holy maiden Eugenia….' [coaelive,+ALS_[Eugenia]:1.197]

clean.tx: Ða wæs sum þegen annanias gehaten. & his wif saphira hi cwædon him betweonan þæt hi woldon bugan to þæra apostola geferrædene namon þa to ræde þæt him wærlicor wære þæt hi sumne dæl heora landes wurþes æthæfdon weald hu him. getimode Com þa se þegen mid feo to þam apostolum. Ða cwæð petrus: annania: deofol bepæhte þine heortan. & þu hæfst alogen þam halgan gast.
clean.tl: There was some nobleman called Ananias and his wife Saphira. They said to each other that they wanted to turn to the apostles' fellowship. (They) agreed that it would be better for them to withhold some part of their land's worth in case something happened to them. Then the nobleman came with riches to the apostles. Then Peter said: Ananias, devil deceived your heart and you have lied to the Holy Ghost.' [ÆCHom I, 22, [004000 (357.88–92)]]

clean.tx: Mid þy ic ða wolde geornlicor þa þing geseon & furðor eode þa geseah ic gyldenne wingeard trumlicne & fæstlicne, & þa twigo his hongodon geond þa columnan Ða wundrode ic þæs swiðe. Wæron in þæm wingearde gyldenu leaf & his hon & his wæstmas wæron cristallum & smaragdus, eac þæt gimcyn mid þæm cristallum ingemong hongode.
clean.tl: When I wanted to see these things more carefully and went further, then I saw a golden vine, strong and firm, and the twigs were hanging over the columns. Then I wondered at this very much. There were golden leaves in the vine bush and the vine's tendrils and fruit were crystal and emerald, and also a gem was hanging there among the crystals.

clean.tx: Eft he frægn, hwæt seo þeod nemned wære, þe heo of cwomon. Ondswarede him mon þæt heo Ongle nemde wæron. Cwæð he: Wel þæt swa mæg: forðon heo ænlice onsyne habbað, & eac swylce gedafonað, þæt heo engla æfenerfeweardas in heofonum sy.
clean.tl: He asked again about the name of the tribe from which they came. Someone answered him that they were called Angles. He said: It may well be so because they have angelic faces and it is only becoming that they will later be angels in heaven.' [Bede 2, [002000 (1.96.21–22)]]

clean.tx: … þe Martinus wæs haten. Wæs he Gode swiðe gecoren on his þeawum. Wæs he in Pannana þære mægðe in woruld cumen, in Arrea ðam tune. Wæs he hwæðre in Italia afeded, in <Ticinan> þære byrig. Wæs he for worulde swiðe godre gebyrde. Wæron his fæder & his modor buta hæðen. Wæs his fæder ærest cyninges þegn, & þa æt nehstan geþah þæt he wæs tribunus, þæt is ealdorman cyninges þegna. Þa sceolde he, sanctus Martinus, nyde beon sona on his giogoðhade on geferræddenne cyninges þegna
clean.tl: … who was called Martin. He was very dear to God in his customs. He has come to the world in the diocese of Pannonia, in the city of Arrea. He was nevertheless brought up in Italy, in the city of Ticinum (Pavia). He was of very good birth to the world. His father and his mother were both heathen. His father was first the king's thane, and then (he) was a tribune, that is the alderman of the king's thanes. Then he, St. Martin, in his youth had to belong to the fellowship of the king's thanes.' [LS17.2, [000200 (1))]–[000800 (10))]]

clean.tx: Com se foresprecena hungur eac swylce hider on Bryttas
clean.tl: Likewise the aforesaid famine reached the Britons.

clean.tx: INTEREA Brettones fames sua praefata magis magisque adficiens, ac famam suae malitiae posteris diuturnam relinquens
clean.tl: Meanwhile the Britons, suffering more and more from the aforesaid famine, and leaving the long-lasting reputation of their malice to the posterity….

clean.tx: Erat autem idem Aedilberct filius Irminrici,
clean.tl: This Ethelbert was the son of Eormenric.

clean.tx: Wæs heo seo cwen sona lustfulliende þære godan foresetenesse & willan þæs iungan. Sende him þa to Cent to Ercenbyrhte þam cyninge, se wæs hyre eames sunu; bæd þæt he hine arwurðlice to Rome onsende
clean.tl: She, the queen, was soon glad about the good purpose and will of the young man. (She) sent him then to Kent to Ercenbyrht the king, he was her uncle's son; (she) asked that he kindly sent him to Rome.' [Bede 5, [042100 (17.452.19–21)]]

clean.tx: And he leop sona cunnigende his feðes, hwæðer he cuðe gan. Eode þa mid blisse binnan þam temple mid þam halgum apostolum, þone hælend herigende. Þa oncneowan hine ealle þe hine cuðon ær, and micclum wundrodon þæs wædlan hæle.
clean.tl: And he soon ran, testing his feet, whether he could walk. (He) went then with glory to the temple with the holy apostles, praising Jesus. Then everyone who had known him recognised him and wondered greatly at the health of the poor man.

clean.tx: Þa gelæhte Petrus hire liþian hand, arærde hi upp hale of þam bedde.
clean.tl: Then Peter took her supple hand, (he) raised her up healthy from the bed.' [ÆLS (Peter's Chair) [002800 (73)]]

clean.tx: Þa geseah he swa þeostre dene ane under him in niþernesse gesette. Geseah he eac feower fyr onæled on þære lyfte noht micle fæce betweoh him tosceaden.
clean.tl: Then he saw a deep valley beneath. He saw also four fires lit in the air not far away from one another.' [Bede 3, [040400 (14.212.20)]–[040500 (14.212.22)]]

clean.tx: Maurus gemette ænne man eft se wæs yfele getawod
clean.tl: Maurus met a man afterwards who was evilly stricken.' [ÆLS[Maur]:283.1661]

clean.tx: And Maurus ða gemette ær he to mynstre come ænne dumbne cnapan ⁊ se wæs creopere eac
clean.tl: and Maurus then met before he came to the monastery a dumb boy and he was a cripple as well.' [ÆLS[Maur]:19.1507–8]

clean.tx: ge seceað þone hælynd þone þe on rode ahangen wæs
clean.tl: You seek the Savior, him, who was hanged on the cross.' [cowsgosp,Mt_[WSCp]:28.5.2139];

clean.tx: Se feorða godspellere is Iohannes Cristes moddrian sunu, se wæs Criste swa leof þæt he hlynode uppan his breoste.
clean.tl: The fourth gospelwriter is John, Christ's aunt's son, who was so dear to Christ that he leaned upon his breast.' [ÆLS_[Mark]:159.3304]

clean.tx: Joop, die nu zijn kamer gaat opruimen!, komt straks buiten spelen.
clean.tl: Joop, who is now going to clean his room!, will come play outside later.

clean.tx: sum wæs arwurðes lifes wer, se wæs mid Godes gife gebledsod & be naman genemned Benedictus, þæt is on Englisc se gebletsoda.
clean.tl: There was a man of honourable life who was blessed with God's gift and called by the name of Benedictus, which is in English “the blessed one”.' [cogregdH,GDPref_2_[H]:94.23.971]

clean.tx: Sum wif hatte Sintice, seo wæs six gear blind
clean.tl: There was a woman called Sintice, who had been blind for six years.' [ÆLS_[Thomas]:263.7705]

clean.tx: On þam þinge ic oncnawe, þæt Benedictus hæfde Paulus gewrixle, se þa þa he þolode scipes forwyrd & lyre eallra þara þinga, þe þæar on wæron, þa onfeng he sylf him to frofre eallra þara lif, þe him mid ferdon.
clean.tl: In which thing I see that Benedict imitated St. Paul: who, when he suffered the wreck of a ship and the loss of all the goods that were on it, then he himself received, for his comfort, the lives of all that were in his company.' [cogregdH,GD_2_[H]:17.141.10.1370]

clean.tx: and Godes sacerdas synd gewuldrode mid þære onwrigennysse Martines forðsiðes, þonne se halga Michahel mid englum underfeng and Maria seo eadiga mid mædenlicum werodum, and neorxnewang gehylt bliðne mid halgum.
clean.tl: and the priests of God are glorified by the revelation of Martin's departure, whom the holy Michael with his angels and blessed Mary with companies of virgins received; whom paradise holdeth, happy among saints.' [ÆLS_[Martin]:1435.6918]

clean.tx: Þa wæs þær sumre neah cyricean mæssepreost, þam wæs nama Florentius, se wæs Florenties ures subdiacones yldra fæder.
clean.tl: Then was there of a nearby church a masspriest who was by name Florentius. He was the father of our subdeacon Florentius.' [cogregdH,GD_2_[H]: 8.117.2.1151]

flagged.tl: Both were adequately educated in matters related to the Church and in the science of the scripture.

flagged.tl: Osred, his son, took over the throne; (he) was an eight-year boy.' [Bede 5, [037800 (16.446.4)]]

flagged.tx: & þa sealde he heom mid his agenre handa ane trywene flascan wines fulle, to þon þæt hi mihton heom þa on heora færelde to underngeweorce habban. Of þære hi druncon, oð þæt hi to rauennam becomon
flagged.tl: and then, with his own hands, he gave them a wooden bottle full of wine, so that they might have that for breakfast during their journey. They drank from it, until they arrived in Ravenna.' (i.e. it lasted them all the way to Ravenna) [GD_1_[C]:9.66.12.742–743]
